posts.title: First class failure scenarios in Java
summary: Checked exceptions can capture failure scenarios in the type signature. This specialized semantic has fallen out of favor to its unchecked counterpart. This leaves the compiler in the blind on potential failures. Contemporary Java allows us to express possible failures in new and better ways.

items.name: zlox
text: A bytecode interpreter for Lox, the language from Crafting Interpreters, written in Zig: a single-pass Pratt compiler, a stack-based VM with closures and classes, and a mark-and-sweep garbage collector.
It adds arrays, continue, file output and wider operands to the book's version, enough to write a Mandelbrot renderer, a raytracer and Game of Life in Lox itself.

items.name: shader-playground
items.text: A browser playground for learning ray tracing on the GPU. Place and drag cubes in a three.js scene, then switch to a full-screen GLSL fragment shader that receives the same scene, and write the raytracer that renders it.

items.name: entitlements
text: Led the build and operation of Miro's entitlement checks: the system that decides, on every guarded action, whether a customer's plan includes the feature. 10k requests per second sustained, more at peak.

Every service depends on it, so it can't be a single point of failure. Entitlements are pushed to a sidecar next to each team's service, which keeps them in memory and refreshes from Kafka or reads a precomputed view in Redis. Shipped in 2024; it covers on/off features, limits (3 boards on the free plan) and AI credit metering.
A change to a huge plan (the free plan has over 20M users) isn't precomputed per customer. One message goes out and sidecars compute the entitlement at read time, so there's no long consistency gap.

items.name: instruqt-sandboxes
text: Sandboxes for hands-on workshops, anything from a single node to a full Kubernetes cluster, provisioned and torn down with Terraform from precomputed plans.

The load comes in spikes: a trainer starts a workshop and thousands of sandboxes spin up at once, on top of CI runs that play through customers' courses. A predictive scheduler warmed sandboxes up ahead of scheduled training dates. I also led and built webhooks for the platform.

items.name: mermaid-multiplayer
items.text: Led research into real-time collaboration for Miro's Mermaid diagrams, which users edit both as code and visually. Showed that the existing OT framework couldn't resolve concurrent visual operations, and wrote the design for multiplayer built on our visual actions with custom conflict resolution.

items.name: mermaid-fuzzer
items.text: A seeded fuzzer for the library that turns visual operations (delete a node, say) into edits of the Mermaid source. It generates valid diagrams, applies random operations, and reports any result that fails to parse or differs from the expected state. A CLI replays a failure from its seed; in CI it catches regressions.
